findings.summary: Low-ticket threshold is not fully unified: the students tab still treats only exactly 1 ticket as low.
findings.evidence: Line 75 counts students with ticketBalance <= 2 and the summary card (line 131, 'チケット残り2枚以下') navigates to the students tab on click, but on that tab line 469-470 use isZero = balance === 0 and isLow = balance === 1. A student with 2 tickets is counted in the card yet shown there with the green (emerald) badge and no label, so the admin cannot see who the counted student is. Business rule states warning at 2, 1, 0. Records (daily-four.md) only claim the summary, today-row colour and booking form were unified, so this is an incomplete fix rather than a regression.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the same threshold on the students tab (e.g. isLow = balance > 0 && balance <= 2 with label '残り{n}回'), ideally through one shared constant used by TeacherDashboard, AddRideModal and ParentPortal, and add an assertion for the 2-ticket card.

findings.summary: The candidate's own dry run reports two error codes the generator classifies as unexpected; adopting r19 as-is will not make the strict check pass.

SOURCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED is 8 (matches the 8 files reviewed here). These are document-index issues from the other session's records, not defects in the registry candidate content.
findings.suggestedFix: Before adoption, index the four progress documents and resolve the README drift through the normal document procedure, then rerun the dry run and require unexpectedCodes to be empty. Do not adopt on the assumption that only the three expected codes remain.

The proposal discloses this under 'limits', so it is not hidden, but after adoption the baseline hash will cover code whose new behaviour no registered test would catch if it regressed (e.g. reverting <=2 to <=1 passes all 211 tests as far as I can tell from the registered suites' fresh results being produced before and after with no dedicated assertion; not exhaustively proven).
findings.suggestedFix: Either register tests for the three behaviours (promote the ad hoc scripts into scripts/ with hashed reports) in r19, or record them as an explicit follow-up item in the registry/progress record so the gap is tracked.

findings.summary: PM-04 and PM-05 are narrower than their names: 'no guidance for other failures' is only exercised on the parent entrance, and PM-05 only checks the admin link.
findings.evidence: Line 71-76 loops over three messages with route {kind:'parent'} only and tests absence of the parent-entrance sentence ('登録されていません。保護者の方は') and the admin link. A bug that showed the admin-entrance guidance paragraph for unrelated errors on #/admin would pass. PM-05 (line 79-80) asserts only that the link is absent before login, not the guidance text. The current component uses one shared condition (LoginScreen.tsx:55) so the behaviour is correct today; mutation testing confirmed the test does fail for six realistic breakages.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat the PM-04 loop for {kind:'admin'} asserting '管理者用の入口には登録されていません' is absent, and in PM-05 also assert the guidance text is absent.

findings.summary: The retry test stubs '../portal' with its own copy of isPortalMismatch, so it does not exercise the real function and its evidence does not hash src/portal.ts.
findings.evidence: Line 17 supplies { DEMO_ENTRY_ID: 'demo', isPortalMismatch: ... } and line 47 hashes only LoginScreen.tsx and the script. The only error used is '認証中断', so the stub always returns false; the test would pass whatever the real implementation did. This is acceptable for UI-07/UI-08 (retry behaviour), and the real function is covered by PM-01..05, but UI-07/08 evidence must not be read as covering the guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: None required; optionally load the real portal.ts as the mismatch test does.

findings.summary: Wrong-entrance detection matches on the Japanese message prefix rather than the server error code.
findings.evidence: isPortalMismatch uses message.startsWith('この入口ではログインできません'). gas/Code.gs:233 and portal.ts:25 both start with that sentence today, and api.ts request() passes json.error through verbatim, so it works. The server code PORTAL_MISMATCH is discarded by request(). If either text is reworded the guidance silently disappears (fails closed: the refusal itself is unaffected). The reviewer-specific PORTAL_MISMATCH text at Code.gs:215 deliberately does not match.
findings.suggestedFix: Longer term, carry the API code on the thrown error and test that instead; or add a test that reads the literal from gas/Code.gs so a rewording is caught.

findings.summary: The guidance block is outside the role="alert" element, so screen readers announce the refusal but not the guidance or the link.
findings.evidence:
Line 54 is

; the guidance

on line 55-61 has no live-region role. Sighted users see both. The link is a real and keyboard reachable.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the refusal and the guidance in one role="alert" container, or give the guidance div role="status".

findings.summary: Day rollover relies on a midnight setTimeout plus visibilitychange only; resume from device sleep with the tab still visible may show the previous day until the delayed timer fires.
findings.evidence: Effect at lines 53-69: timer re-arms itself to the next local midnight, listener is visibilitychange. Cleanup clears the pending timer and removes the listener (verified by reading; no leak, safe under StrictMode double invocation, an early firing re-arms correctly, setting the same string does not re-render). Browsers may pause timers during system suspend and visibilitychange does not fire if the tab stayed visible. Records state a real overnight run on the public page was not performed.
findings.suggestedFix: Also listen for window 'focus' and 'pageshow', or add a low-frequency interval check; optional.

findings.summary: RETRY-UI-01 evidence is a wrapper generated by prepare_r19.py from a stdout log, and trace-ui results.json has no execution timestamp.

Same practice as r18 according to the script comment.
findings.suggestedFix: Have the test scripts write their own hashed, timestamped reports.
